Hello everyone,

My name is Stich and I would like to say a very special thank you to the amazing team at PDSA Birmingham.

On 14 July, I was at the hospital withpn my mum when she suddenly collapsed. I was frightened because she is my whole world. But all of you rushed to help her straight away, took such good care of her, and made sure she was safe.

I may only be a little dog, but if I could speak, I would tell you how grateful I am. Thank you for looking after my mum with so much kindness and compassion, and for taking care of me too.

Because of you, my tail is wagging again. You are true heroes, and I will never forget what you did for my mum.

With lots of love and happy tail wags,

Stich  🐾❤️

Heavily subsidised pet care. PDSA are amazing but seriously need funding to keep up their brilliant work. There's a cat crisis where I live. I've taken in 5 stray cats and feed many more. I wouldn't be able to do what I do without the compassion of PDSA and help of neighbours. PDSA desperately need funding for more vets, more registrations, better segregation of cat v dog seating, shorter emergency call wait times and more appointment slots and more payment options (preferably to spread the cost if needed).
PDSA also have excellent disability support and reasonable adjustments for registered owners. PDSA enable people with disabilities to have nominees.
The reception staff always try their best within the limited resources they have available. All in all, Thank you to everyone at PDSA

Serious concerns! You would actually think the people who work at this charity branch are there to help pets & their owners in need in specifically a healthcare environment. They also con and force you out of charging excessively for what they call a ‘voluntary contribution’ being a charity…

Instead on numerous occasions there has been shocking behaviour from the receptionists - observing and witnessing being treated according to ethnicity.

Furthermore- my concerns with them keep growing, I’ve been told to PUT MY CAT TO SLEEP BASED ON ONE ‘physical examination! The vet wouldn’t even give me a chance to talk & kept trying to push me to go ‘private’ why would I be registered here in the first place if I could? They also use the last resort as the first easily said option of putting pets to sleep so easily rather then trying to save their lives even in the slightest medical issue. How is it best to ‘put them to sleep’ they should be doing their jobs by further investigating as they have the facilities to treat sick animals.

How can they have their jobs in such place? it makes no sense, the way they talk to others!
There are many people out there deserving of these jobs & the wrong type of people are employed who yell at others and have no form of communication skills.

The charity needs a serious look into their staff members and the impact it’s causing to pets & their owners as soon as possible. Everyone who’s experienced neglect from this place should formally raise their complaints further.

Extremely disappointed with my experience at PDSA Aston today. I was left waiting for over an hour due to Richard, the admin staff member, failing to check my pet in. He was free when I arrived at the desk to check in but chose to ignore me and make a phone call instead of helping. I’m heavily pregnant, and this lack of consideration was appalling. During the wait, my dog Cookie urinated in the waiting area. When I mentioned it to Richard, he simply pointed to a mop, offering no further assistance.

Thankfully, a kind vet noticed my struggle and helped clean up, but the damage was done. The worst part came when I went to pay for Cookie’s medication. Laura, who was dispensing the medication at the time, asked if I’d be making a voluntary donation today. I explained I usually do donate but I couldn’t today and she proceeded to lecture me about how the vets rely on donations. I said I would pay for my dogs medication but that was all. After collecting my payment she then rudely pointed out I hadn’t donated since February. I was shocked by her passive aggressive attitude and complete lack of professionalism. I responded by informing Laura that I wouldn't be making a voluntary donation after the appalling experience I encountered today.
I have never experienced such condescending behaviour at the PDSA before. I have made a formal complaint about my experience today, I am currently awaiting the managers response. Hopefully this will be dealt with professionally and timely.
